Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The agent made a fundamental error in interpreting the term "pure dominant." In genetics, a "pure" dominant plant is homozygous dominant (RR), not heterozygous (Rr). The agent incorrectly assumed the round-seed parent was heterozygous (Rr), leading to the conclusion of a 1:1 phenotypic ratio. If the parent is truly pure dominant (RR) and crossed with a wrinkled plant (rr), all offspring will be heterozygous (Rr) and exhibit the dominant round phenotype. Therefore, the correct answer is that they will always produce round seeds.
